html:
The Frankish kingdoms were the realms of the Franks, a Germanic people who took over Roman Gaul and built the largest post Roman state in western Europe. The chart runs from the accession of Clovis in 481 to the Treaty of Verdun in 843.

Clovis, of the Merovingian dynasty, united the Franks, beat the last Roman ruler in Gaul and the Visigoths, and became a Catholic at the baptism usually dated to 496. That choice tied the Franks to the Church of Rome and to the Gallo-Roman population they ruled. On a king's death the land was split among his sons, so Merovingian Francia was often several kingdoms at once.

Real power passed to the mayors of the palace. One of them, Charles Martel, stopped a raid from al-Andalus near Tours in 732. His son Pepin took the crown in 751 with the Pope's blessing, founding the Carolingian line.

Pepin's son Charlemagne conquered the Lombards in Italy, the Saxons and Bavaria, and was crowned emperor in Rome on Christmas Day 800. His court sponsored schools, new copies of Latin texts and a clear new handwriting. After his son Louis the Pious died, Louis's sons fought, and at Verdun they divided the realm in three. The western part became France; the eastern part grew into the Holy Roman Empire.
sum: The Frankish kingdoms were the realms of the Franks, a Germanic people who took over Roman Gaul and built the largest post Roman state in western Europe. The chart runs from the accession of Clovis in 481 to the Treaty of Verdun in 843.
